garbage can be recycled such as plastic bags and films, and foam. These
items do not go in your recycling cart, to learn how to recycle them visit
kingcounty.gov/whatdoidowith or kirklandwa.gov/beyondthecart.

WHAT DO I DO WITH...?
Hazardous Waste
Scan for more info
If the label includes words such as danger, poison, caution, or toxic, it’s likely
hazardous waste and needs special disposal at drop-off locations.
Your business may be eligible for no-fee hazardous waste disposal up to four
times a year. To qualify, your business must be a Small Quantity Generator,
meaning you produce and store only a small quantity of hazardous material.
Call 206-296-4692 or visit kingcountyhazwastewa.gov.
Fluorescent Bulbs/Tubes + HIDs
Recycle up to 10 mercury-containing bulbs and tubes daily for free through
LightRecycle (lightrecycle.org). LEDs, halogen and incandescents are not
recyclable in your cart but can go in the garbage.
Options for paint recycling
Latex and oil-based paint can be recycled through a
statewide program. Visit paintcare.org/WA for details
and limits, and to find locations near you.
Electronics
Computers, monitors, TVs + tablets
Recycle computers, tablets, e-readers, monitors, TVs, and laptops for free by
dropping off at an E-Cycle Washington location (ecyclewa.org).
